placements.title: App Composer patch notes
placements.caption: Proof, please. The release record should say what changed, name the revision and let someone do the task on the live site. That’s how we work on App Composer.
placements.alt: Workshop photo and bold App Composer type ask for source, release and live check. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show the real diff, the exact released revision and the affected action in a single short.

placements.title: Pick a door
placements.caption: Pick a door. The office one looks trustworthy, which feels like a warning. Ten endings, and you can write your own.
placements.alt: Three strange doors in a violet corridor ask which entrance to choose. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show three physical doors. Cut to a real played ending without spoiling the other two rooms.

placements.title: LoftwahFM after midnight
placements.caption: LoftwahFM after midnight. Here’s the sleeve I’d leave next to a late-night mix. What’s the first sound you hear when you see it?
placements.alt: A stripped speaker and copper coils sit under an orange slash of light on the LoftwahFM sleeve. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use an approved LoftwahFM track or a new original ident. Keep the sleeve first and the audio credit clear.

placements.title: Tech hot-take bingo
placements.caption: I heard “clear the cache” before breakfast. Mark the tech takes you’ve heard today, then send the board to whoever said them.
placements.alt: A punk gig flyer turns nine familiar tech takes into a bingo board. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Capture five taps in the actual app. Let the bingo reveal play and finish by showing the owner’s editable board.

placements.title: App Composer field manual
placements.caption: Keep the source. Leave a way back in. App Composer is an open-source workshop for getting something useful live and returning to it.
placements.alt: A small workshop and wall hook sit under App Composer field-manual lettering. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Start with the key on the hook and cross-cut to a real second edit in Creator Hub.

placements.title: Pull another
placements.caption: There’s a particular second before the foil catches the light. That’s the feeling we’re chasing in Foilbury. Here’s an original collector’s print.
placements.alt: An original gold collector’s card emerges from a burnt-orange foil pack. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use a real rights-cleared Foilbury pack opening alongside the art. Capture the actual foil reveal.

placements.title: Forms with the door shut
placements.caption: A PDF you can fill in your browser. Paperwork keeps the edit local. Try the fictional lab form and download the finished file.
placements.alt: A press and orange shutter illustrate Paperwork’s local PDF editing. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Capture one form field, a mark and the local export of the actual fictional sample.

placements.title: Nine games that made me
placements.caption: Nine games that made me. I want the embarrassing one in the middle. Make your own exhibition and post it with no explanation.
placements.alt: Nine illustrated game exhibits in a violet museum. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Reveal the nine objects in rhythm, then open the actual Top Nine editor and fill one square.

placements.title: Build things you can take apart
placements.caption: A diagram earns its keep if someone can take it apart, change it and show what moved. That’s why we publish editable LDraw source with the App Composer atlas.
placements.alt: An exploded physical brick machine illustrates the App Composer LDraw atlas. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Record an actual editable LDraw scene coming apart, then replace one module and save.

placements.title: Leave more doors open
placements.caption: Remembering Aaron Swartz. A healthier web makes it easier for someone else to read, learn, publish and build. Leave one more useful door open.
placements.alt: A public book drop at dusk with a quiet dedication to Aaron Swartz. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Let the artwork sit still. Pair it with the Internet Archive memorial as its own post.

placements.title: Pick a side
placements.caption: Ruby or Python. One choice and one sentence to defend it. I’ll accept “the thing I can still maintain on Monday.”
placements.alt: Orange arcade scorecard pits Ruby against Python. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Open on the two silhouettes. Hit the VS on a coin-clink. Hold the two choices long enough to read.

placements.title: Choose your main
placements.caption: The Legacy Monolith enters the arena. Special move: still works. Name your main and the bug you’d never send them to fix.
placements.alt: Pixel-art computer cabinet fighter called The Legacy Monolith. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Scan the fighter like a loading screen, then hold on Still works as the soundtrack cuts.

placements.title: I’m a Durable Object
placements.caption: I’m a Durable Object, apparently. For a group game, one named object can coordinate shared state. What would your infrastructure card say?
placements.alt: An orbital library on a fictional Cloudflare Durable Object collectible. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Glide through the rings and land on the educational fact. Read without sound.

placements.title: Defend your rankings
placements.caption: Which tool is S tier for you, and what’s it actually good at? The duck will hear arguments for production, weekends and everything in between.
placements.alt: A panel of Roman judges ranks a rubber duck in an arena. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Slow zoom on the duck. Stamp an S on a separate title frame. Leave time for a reply.

placements.title: Pick your curse
placements.caption: Unlimited tokens without internet, or unlimited internet without AI. Pick one, meet its tiny consequence and keep your curse card.
placements.alt: Split game-show poster sets a library against a wall of modems. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Both sides appear at once. Use a one-second blackout between two replies, never flash rapidly.

placements.title: The nine realms of dev
placements.caption: Chaotic good is fixing prod before anyone notices. True neutral leaves a line in the runbook so the next person can do it too. What’s your class?
placements.alt: A woodcut deploy engineer holds a chaotic-good scroll. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Reveal the character class, then cut to a quiet close-up of a marked-up runbook.

placements.title: A very specific internet person
placements.caption: Local-first night owl. Identifying marks include a README, seven terminal tabs and a mistrust of silent sync. Name a specimen you know.
placements.alt: An owl made of keyboard feathers, preserved in amber like a museum specimen. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use a field guide page turn. End on the name and habitat, without rarity statistics.

placements.title: You ship tomorrow
placements.caption: You have to ship tomorrow. Give me your agent, app, data and runtime choices. Then tell me who owns the account and comes back for the second edit.
placements.alt: An exploded orbital workshop with separate agent, app, data and runtime modules. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Assemble four modules, then pause on the owner question. Use a second slide for the technical detail.

placements.title: The budget is twenty bucks
placements.caption: Your fictional hosting budget is $20 a month. What do you keep, what can wait and which line item will ruin the receipt?
placements.alt: Thermal receipt on a retro shopping show asking what to keep within a $20 scenario. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Cash register sound into a frozen receipt. Add the scenario label before the number appears.

placements.title: Red flag or green flag?
placements.caption: Forty-seven tabs. Red flag, green flag, or a perfectly respectable search strategy? The court will take evidence.
placements.alt: A lurid tabloid courtroom asks for a ruling on 47 browser tabs. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Two beats of evidence, one gavel, then leave viewers room to explain their ruling.

placements.title: Love at first token
placements.caption: My type is low latency and easy to leave. What actually matters when you choose an agent: speed, its tools, or the way it handles a long project?
placements.alt: Two chrome terminals on stools in a 1970s dating-show poster. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Slow pan between terminals. Cut to the real question as a wordless applause cue lands.

placements.title: The Legacy Necromancer
placements.caption: The Legacy Necromancer has a very particular skill: opening a project everyone forgot and getting it running. Tag the person you’d trust with the keys.
placements.alt: A wizard revives a steam-powered server on a midnight railway platform. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Display as an animated card reveal with a tiny fluorescent status light, then hold on the class name.

placements.title: Guess the model
placements.caption: Try reading three outputs before you see who made them. What would make one worth using in your project? Mark your answer before the reveal.
placements.alt: An intelligence dossier with three anonymous output sheets. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Publish an actual blind sample only after saving exact prompts, model records and comparable settings. The art teaser needs no score.

placements.title: Design crime scene
placements.caption: The button has entered a witness protection programme. Before you blame the user, give them a visible action and try your flow on a phone.
placements.alt: A design test lab investigates an almost invisible button. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Freeze the bad contrast example. Reveal a deliberate corrected button and verbalise what changed.

placements.title: One must go
placements.caption: Music, games, code, the web. One has to go. I’m mostly interested in the terrible argument you make afterwards.
placements.alt: Four personal technology objects under dark awards-show spotlights. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show the four choices, pause, dim one light. Invite replies with what they would sacrifice.

placements.title: You can hear this picture
placements.caption: You can hear this image. What sound would you put in a museum of the early internet?
placements.alt: Ivory CRT and dial-up modem on a dusty late-night desktop. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Make an original modem-like synth riff and caption it. Let the viewer guess before naming it.

placements.title: What year did the web go public?
placements.caption: When did CERN put the World Wide Web software into the public domain? Guess before opening the link.
placements.alt: Retro vertical TV quiz card asks when the web went public. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Three-second hold on the question, then reveal 30 April 1993 and credit CERN on frame.

placements.title: Which internet raised you?
placements.caption: Which internet raised you? Forums, feeds, or group chats? Give me one thing from that era we should bring into the next one.
placements.alt: A hand finds old internet mementos in a peach time capsule. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Hold the archive still, then cut between three eras with actual sound design. No fake archive footage.

placements.title: Developer confessions
placements.caption: I wrote the TODO in 2018. It’s still load-bearing. Give us a confession with the company and names left out.
placements.alt: A punk print has a developer whispering at a CRT confessional. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Start with a still whisper. Read the one-line confession and cut before it becomes a lecture.

placements.title: Hot take factory
placements.caption: Some meetings should be README files. Which meeting would you replace with one clear decision and something you can run?
placements.alt: Industrial stamping machine prints a hot take about meetings and README files. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show a blank page turning into one plain record: owner, decision, next move.

placements.title: Internet World Cup
placements.caption: Terminal or GUI. Eight familiar tools, seven picks, one local champion. Back your champion and see who survives.
placements.alt: A cable-connector trophy presides over Terminal versus GUI. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Set sound to a muted crowd swell, hold on both names, then let viewers play the seven-match bracket.

placements.title: The million-dollar question
placements.caption: A year of free time or a million dollars. What would be the first project you actually started?
placements.alt: A TV game show offers a free year against a million dollars as a hypothetical. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use two quiet spotlight reveals and end on the first-project question.

placements.title: Software villain origin story
placements.caption: The Cache Warden was told to clear it one last time. Every maintainer has a villain origin story. What’s yours?
placements.alt: A violet noir comic cover features a fictional keeper of the cache. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Single panel reveal, then a joke in one frame of comic lettering.

placements.title: Assemble your edge squad
placements.caption: You get three powers for a tiny multiplayer project: run code, hold state, store media. Which one do you design around first?
placements.alt: An original comic team personifies compute, state and storage. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Reveal each of the three characters, then cut to a real source-linked architecture slide.

placements.title: This should not exist
placements.caption: The Cancellation Club. A club for people who wanted to stay home. The first question in the brief is “who’s doing this by hand now?”
placements.alt: A fake 1980s magazine pitch for a cancellation service. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show the imaginary pitch as a prop, then turn it over to a real one-page build brief.

placements.title: Draft your agent squad
placements.caption: Your squad gets five slots. I’m taking a researcher, designer, builder, reviewer and releaser. Who keeps the brief with the project?
placements.alt: An original crew manifest with five software-work roles. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Introduce roles with five distinct silhouettes. Finish with a real example of a handoff and its review.

placements.title: Wrong answers only
placements.caption: What happens inside a database? Wrong answers only. I think someone puts the rows back in order after we go home.
placements.alt: An old textbook cover imagines tiny furniture and a kettle inside a database cabinet. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use mock classroom narration over the art. Put Wrong Answers Only on the first shot.

placements.title: The website is on trial
placements.caption: The fictional website is on trial. The charge is hiding its main button. Show me an example you own and the one thing you want visitors to do.
placements.alt: Courtroom sketch puts a fictional website’s missing button on trial. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Use a clearly labeled fictional layout, then show a real actionable before/after with the owner’s permission.

placements.title: My year online
placements.caption: Three things about your year online: the discovery, the obsession, the thing you’re finally going to build. Put those in your recap.
placements.alt: A cream and orange collage arranges old cassette and recording hardware around a year-in-review prompt. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Treat each of the three answers as its own title movement. Use volunteered answers and original audio.

placements.title: Ghosts in the dependency tree
placements.caption: My build’s fictional record is Ghosts in the Dependency Tree. Name yours and pick the genre. I want the liner notes too.
placements.alt: Album art with entangled wires and frosted audio gear under an original title. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Make an eight-second station ident with an original sound and a slow start-to-finish sleeve turn.

placements.title: What would you build?
placements.caption: What would you build if building software was the easy part? Tell me who it helps and what they’d do with it. That’s a better brief than a feature list.
placements.alt: A maker with a notebook looks over a canyon of imaginary inventions. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Open on a real problem in the maker’s voice. Reveal the poster at the end and ask for one concrete idea.

placements.title: The internet needs this
placements.caption: The internet needs this. Name one little thing you still fix manually, preferably the one nobody thinks is worth building.
placements.alt: A World’s Fair patent poster shows a machine assembling a project archive. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Present three fictional micro-inventions like a public science fair. End on one live implementation when it exists.

placements.title: App Composer patch notes
placements.caption: Show the change, name the revision, do the thing on the live site. The App Composer release receipt.
placements.alt: Workshop photo and bold App Composer type ask for source, release and live check. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show the real diff, the exact released revision and the affected action in a single short.

placements.title: Pick a door
placements.caption: Three entrances, ten endings. I took the door that looked like a normal office. That was a mistake.
placements.alt: Three strange doors in a violet corridor ask which entrance to choose. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Show three physical doors. Cut to a real played ending without spoiling the other two rooms.

placements.title: Tech hot-take bingo
placements.caption: Someone said ‘just rewrite it’ at 8:07. Turn your dev feed into a playable bingo board.
placements.alt: A punk gig flyer turns nine familiar tech takes into a bingo board. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Capture five taps in the actual app. Let the bingo reveal play and finish by showing the owner’s editable board.

placements.title: Forms with the door shut
placements.caption: Paperwork is a local PDF editor in the browser. Try it with the fictional lab form and take the finished file with you.
placements.alt: A press and orange shutter illustrate Paperwork’s local PDF editing. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Capture one form field, a mark and the local export of the actual fictional sample.

placements.title: The internet needs this
placements.caption: Tell me the smallest thing you still do by hand that the internet should have a tool for.
placements.alt: A World’s Fair patent poster shows a machine assembling a project archive. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Present three fictional micro-inventions like a public science fair. End on one live implementation when it exists.

placements.title: App Composer field manual
placements.caption: What can you still touch after the agent chat closes? Source, ownership and a working release are good places to start.
placements.alt: A small workshop and wall hook sit under App Composer field-manual lettering. App Composer Internet Workshop.
placements.shortBrief: Start with the key on the hook and cross-cut to a real second edit in Creator Hub.
